newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open sharply lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open sharply lower on consolidation.

text.p: French shares fell at Wednesday's open, giving up all the ground they gained on Tuesday, on profit-taking triggered by Wall Street's overnight 1.12 percent retreat, traders said.
The correction was expected and would allow the market to consolidate before attempting a fresh attack on the all-time high of 2,360.98 hit on February 1994.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 31.88 points or 1.36 percent at 2,317.23 at 0920 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,321 from 2,352 on Tuesday's close.
The market is well supported, with hopes of an interest rate cut as early as Thursday.

Engineering group Alcatel Alsthom fell 2.72 percent to 462.2 francs on news the government had suspended the privatisation of electronics firm Thomson SA as the Privatisation Commission had not approved the sale of part of the group to Daewoo.
"The chances (for Alcatel) have got to be increased by this, if they can come up with a different offer," said a broker.
Analysts said investors were nervous about the cost of taking over Thomson for Alcatel, which lost to Lagardere when the government made its original choice of buyer.

Lagardere and Thomson-CSF were suspended until further notice. The government had preferred Lagardere's bid for Thomson, which included a sale of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
